findings.evidence: The pointwise API exposes `cauchyPVAt` and value lemmas at `CauchyPrincipalValue.lean:109`, `:154`, `:159`, and `:165`; `rg` in the new file finds only `HasCauchyPV`, `hasCauchyPV_iff`, `.intro`, `CauchyPVExists`, bridges, and zero/const/congr lemmas at `CauchyPrincipalValueOn.lean:86`, `:97`, `:110`, `:121`, `:138`, `:156`, `:176`, `:185`, `:205`, with no set-level value or uniqueness declaration.
findings.fix: Add the canonical `limUnder` value and the corresponding equality, uniqueness, and existence-to-canonical-value lemmas, or otherwise expose a named uniqueness theorem sufficient to use `CauchyPVExists` as a value-bearing interface.
findings.issue: `HasCauchyPV` is exposed as the roadmap-level existence-and-value predicate, but the set-level API has no `cauchyPV`, `HasCauchyPV.cauchyPV_eq`, `HasCauchyPV.unique`, or `CauchyPVExists.hasCauchyPV_cauchyPV` analogue.

summary: The public predicate now has some operation lemmas, but it still lacks the value/uniqueness API expected for an existence-and-value principal-value interface. Downstream users cannot recover a canonical set-level PV value from `CauchyPVExists` or prove two `HasCauchyPV` witnesses give the same value without unfolding and redoing limit uniqueness.
